title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v25
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Add a new set of profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and a reporting ETL pipeline for Benchmark Lab (v25). Motivation: recent infra and runtime changes (kernel selection + KV cache improvements) have changed performance characteristics; we need refreshed baselines and a reliable reporting pipeline to track regressions across GPU types and quantization profiles. What this PR does: 1) Adds representative workload runners for conversational, instruction, and embedding workloads with configurable sequence distributions and batching knobs. 2) Adds profiling baselines for cold-start and steady-state across T4, A10, and H100 instance profiles. Baselines include standardized input sets and collection hooks. 3) Adds a lightweight ETL pipeline (ci/benchmark-lab.yml + reporting/etl.yml) that uploads metrics to the benchmarking store and generates weekly reports. 4) Adds docs and a benchmark CI job that runs a small smoke-profile on PRs to catch obvious regressions. Notes on safety and cost: nightly profiling is limited to a small sample to avoid large GPU spend; full profiling is gated behind linear tasks and infra approvals. Migration: existing baselines v1..v24 are left intact; this is additive. See the changed files list for details. Checklist: - [x] Add workload runners and config - [x] Add profiling baselines and scripts - [x] Add reporting ETL and CI integration - [x] Update docs and release notes - [x] Add tests: smoke-profile CI and unit tests for metric formatting Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. Rollout: merged to main; nightly job created but not scheduled until infra credit approval.
